issuer.industry: Digital infrastructure engineering, deployment, and maintenance services

dimensions.name: Revenue growth and durability
dimensions.judgment: Growth and contract coverage are strong, but acquisitions and discretionary customer budgets reduce durability.

dimensions.name: Profitability and cash flow
dimensions.judgment: Adjusted cash metrics are positive, but GAAP earnings weakened and operating cash flow lagged the company-defined measure.

dimensions.name: Market and competitive position
assumptions: No independent market-share dataset is included.
dimensions.judgment: Long-duration infrastructure demand is attractive, but customers control project volumes and spending.

dimensions.name: Valuation quality
dimensions.judgment: A reproducible fully diluted enterprise value and peer set have not yet been established.

dimensions.name: Debt and balance-sheet resilience
dimensions.judgment: The IPO reduces leverage, but substantial debt and interest sensitivity remain.

dimensions.name: Use of proceeds
dimensions.judgment: Primary capital improves the balance sheet, but nearly all proceeds repay debt rather than fund measurable growth.

dimensions.name: Insider selling, lock-up, and dilution
assumptions: Future exchanges and incentive awards are not fully modeled.
dimensions.judgment: No base secondary sale is positive, but the Up-C structure and continuing-owner position create dilution and cash-flow complexity.

dimensions.name: Governance and shareholder rights
dimensions.judgment: Minority public voting power and extensive Oaktree rights create material governance concerns.

dimensions.name: Legal and regulatory risk
dimensions.judgment: A dedicated claim-level legal and regulatory review is still required.

dimensions.name: Disclosure quality and consistency
dimensions.judgment: Disclosure is detailed, but the Up-C structure and non-GAAP cash metric add interpretive complexity.

red_flags.title: Profitability weakened
red_flags.explanation: GAAP earnings fell and Q1 2026 moved to a loss.

red_flags.title: IPO proceeds mainly repay debt
red_flags.explanation: The balance sheet improves, but substantial debt remains.

red_flags.title: Continuing owners retain control
red_flags.explanation: Public holders begin with minority voting power and complex related-party rights.

positive_signals.title: Revenue growth and MSA coverage
positive_signals.explanation: Revenue grew and most 2025 revenue was under multi-year MSAs.

positive_signals.title: Base offering is primary
positive_signals.explanation: The base shares were issued by the company rather than sold by existing holders.

positive_signals.title: Debt reduction is quantified
positive_signals.explanation: The filing clearly shows expected post-offering debt reduction.

unknowns: A reproducible fully diluted enterprise value and peer valuation set have not yet been established.
The legal and regulatory dimension requires a dedicated claim-level review.
This draft does not model all future LLC-interest exchanges, incentive-plan awards, or Tax Receivable Agreement cash payments.

evidence.location: Consolidated Statements of Operations and MD&A
evidence.extracted_fact: Revenue rose from $997.996m in 2024 to $1,154.857m in 2025; $64.8m of 2025 revenue came from acquired businesses.
Multi-year MSAs represented about 92% of 2025 revenue; engineering and maintenance represented about 59%.

evidence.location: Financial statements, MD&A, and Non-GAAP Financial Measures
evidence.extracted_fact: Net income fell from $28.280m in 2024 to $6.214m in 2025; Q1 2026 recorded a $13.158m loss. Company-defined 2025 Free Cash Flow was $91.093m, while operating cash flow was $12.3m.

Term loans and revolver borrowings were $655.875m and $63.0m at March 31, 2026; pro forma after the IPO they were $426.875m and $13.0m. About $279.2m of net proceeds was allocated mainly to debt repayment.
ITG offered 19,512,196 Class A shares at $16.00; the base offering was primary, with an underwriter option for additional company shares.
Continuing owners retained about 62.45% of voting power. Oaktree may nominate six directors while holding at least 40% of voting power, with declining rights down to 5%.
TRA participants are expected to receive 85% of certain realized tax benefits, while ITG expects to retain 15%.
Customers generally have no obligation to assign specific work volumes, and their capital or operating budgets may change quickly.
